how: We read the website of every Portland wedding videographer listed on Lazo (94 listings, 70 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: brand and music-video producers, a photo booth company, DJs and planners listed as videographers, a one-stop portrait shop, and a site whose text was still placeholder lorem ipsum. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: Rain is likely outside July through September; how do you protect gear and audio at a wet outdoor ceremony, and have you filmed one?
Is ceremony and toast audio recorded on lapel mics and a board feed, or just the camera?
When do the highlight film and the full edit arrive, and are raw files included?

picks.name: Lauren Laskin Films
picks.blurb: Lauren Laskin blends digital, Super 8 and 16mm film into documentary wedding films and has shot more than 150 weddings since 2018. Oregon Wedding Day named her Best Videographer in 2024 and 2025, and she travels across the PNW and nationwide.

picks.name: Watertown Films
picks.blurb: Watertown Films says wedding videography is not about trendy edits or staged scenes but about capturing the energy of the day as it felt. With decades of collective experience, the team has filmed hundreds of weddings from candlelit ceremonies in Oregon to vows in the hills of Spain, and the highlight film is only the start of what it delivers.

picks.name: Casperson Productions
picks.blurb: Dane Casperson personally shoots every wedding Casperson Productions takes on, with a small team behind him and what he calls a ridiculous focus on quality. Down to earth, Portland-based, and happy to fly anywhere on the west coast.

picks.name: Taylor and Madye Photography
picks.blurb: Taylor and Madye are a Portland photography duo who also offer video and film, so one team covers both sides of the day. Eleven years of Portland weddings, both of them working in tandem at every one, serving Oregon, Washington and worldwide.

picks.name: Alesia Films
picks.blurb: Alesia Films started after its founder made a wedding film for her mom and stepdad from iPhone footage in September 2018 and saw what it meant to the whole family. Portland photo and video rooted in vintage film mediums and an authentic, documentary style.

picks.name: Portland Event Films
picks.blurb: Cinematic wedding videography from Milwaukie, with wedding packages, elopement video, highlight films and documentary edits each listed on the site. Portland Event Films says its booking process is straightforward and personalized, with transparency a point of pride.

picks.name: JM Weddings LLC
picks.blurb: Julian McFadden's JM Weddings is a photography and videography team based in the Portland area and available across the Hawaiian Islands, serving Oregon, Washington, Hawaii and beyond. What sets them apart, in their words, is photo and video working seamlessly as one.

picks.name: Solidcaptures
picks.blurb: SolidCaptures makes cinematic wedding films out of the Portland area and says it wants to celebrate with you on the day, not just film it. Pricing is build-your-own: the packages give structure, but everything is customizable.

picks.name: Forever Ties DJ, Photography and Video
picks.blurb: Founded by An Cortes, Forever Ties PDX bundles wedding cinematography and photography with DJ, officiant and 360 photo booth services, and says it has filmed and photographed hundreds of weddings. The team lists more than 10 years in film, and photographer Ben has over 17 years.

picks.name: Atelier Pictures
picks.blurb: Jonathan of Atelier Pictures got the photography bug at 19 in Nepal with a film camera and some 20 years later runs a 4K video production and photography studio in Portland with a specialty in documentaries. Weddings are one of the studio's listed services alongside that documentary work.
